newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's June c/a deficit shrinks to $361.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's June c/a deficit shrinks to $361.4 mln.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit narrowed to $361.4 million in June from a $1.31 billion shortfall a year earlier, preliminary figures released by the central Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Monday.
Note: figures are in millions of US dollars
The deficit totalled $10.3 billion for the first half of this year, against $9.82 billion a year before, the central bank said in a statement.

The bank attributed the reduced current account deficit in June to strong growth in heavy industrial and chemical exports, which led to a trade surplus of $264.6 million, compared to a deficit of $655.1 million a year ago.
This marked the first monthly trade surplus since December 1995. The trade deficit in the first half widened to $6.06 billion, compared to a deficit of $5.64 billion a year earlier.
Free-on-board exports rose 11.6 percent year-on-year, while imports increased 2.9 percent.
Customs cleared exports of heavy industrial and chemical goods rose 8.9 percent in June to $8.33 billion, while that of light industrial products gained 6.1 percent to $3.14 billion, the bank said.
Letters of credit received in June edged down 0.8 percent to $5.89 billion from a year ago.
Customs-cleared imports of raw materials rose 4.1 percent to $6.12 billion in June, while imports of food and consumer goods dropped 7.7 percent to $1.33 billion.
The bank said the current account deficit grew in the first half, pressured by the increasing trade deficit and invisible trade deficit.
Increases in overseas travel and transportation expenses were largely responsible for a $600.5 million invisible trade deficit in June and $3.90 billion in the first half .
The Bank of Korea had earlier forecast this year's current account deficit at $17 billion, compared with a $23.72 billion shortfall in 1996.
